key_facts: The Project Manager proposed that the remote control should only be used for the television and not include lighting adaptive features.
The Industrial Designer suggested using a battery for the remote control and two programmable chips for software functionalities and communication, with the communication being done through infrared.
The User Interface mentioned that the remote control should be small and have a feature to beep when looking for it.
The Marketing team suggested that the remote control should have a limited vocabulary speech recognition system similar to mobile phones.
The Marketing team proposed that the remote control should support multiple languages for teletext, allowing users to select their preferred language.
The Industrial Designer mentioned that the remote control should be designed to anticipate future changes in television technology, such as digital systems and internet access.
The Marketing team indicated that the remote control should be slim and small, and that users might be willing to pay a little more for comfort and extra features.
The Project Manager stated that the remote control should not include teletext functionality due to its outdated nature and the popularity of the internet.
The Industrial Designer suggested using a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) for functionalities, which can be programmed as needed.
The Marketing team mentioned that the remote control should not be designed to function as a PDA, focusing instead on the remote control itself.
